briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. Welcome to the climate briefing for November 9, 2026. Today, the world's attention is on the 31st Conference of the Parties to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31), which opened in Antalya, Türkiye. There is an urgent and ongoing call for concrete action and solutions amidst the deepening climate crisis.

sections.title: 🌍 31st Conference of the Parties to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31) Opens: Urgent Call for Action
sections.content: The 31st Conference of the Parties to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31) opened today in Antalya, Türkiye, and will run until the 20th, with world leaders gathering for critical climate crisis talks [3, 7, 111, 148, 151]. This conference marks the 10th anniversary of the Paris Agreement's entry into force and serves as a crucial platform to accelerate its implementation and discuss the transition from 'pledges' to 'action.' South Korea is actively participating, with Global Climate and Environment Ambassador Kang Keum-sil attending as a special presidential envoy [2, 9, 16, 23]. The UN Secretary-General warned that the world has entered 'a new era of climate extremes' and urged greenhouse gas reductions. The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) also anticipates 2026 to be one of the four warmest years on record, with the conference opening after a year of catastrophic extreme weather [10, 112, 113, 114, 119, 141, 161, 163, 164, 165]. COP31 leaders acknowledged the difficulty of curbing the 1.5-degree global warming limit but called for accelerated climate action. A wide range of agendas will be addressed, including climate justice, a ministerial roundtable on Health Day, and the launch of the 'Belem-Antalya Mechanism' for a 'just transition' [13, 108, 129, 130, 131, 138, 139, 147, 152, 154, 156, 158, 168, 169]. However, challenges also exist, such as the absence of the United States, geopolitical factors, and Canada's advocacy for fossil fuel expansion [115, 157, 159, 167].

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis: Unprecedented Changes and Their Impacts
sections.content: The Earth is experiencing climate change at an unprecedented rate. This year, the global average temperature ranked 4th highest on record, while greenhouse gas concentrations, sea levels, and ocean heat content all reached new peaks [26, 28, 127, 165]. This brings us closer to the 1.5-degree global warming limit, with regional warming worldwide already reaching up to 94% [25, 118]. 'Unprecedented,' 'extreme,' and 'worst-case' phenomena are intensifying [5]. Climate change is exacerbating severe urban flooding [110] and profoundly impacting ecosystems, such as increasing the female ratio of sea turtles to over 70%, deepening sex ratio imbalances [8]. Domestically, concerns are growing over the yield and quality of crops like Miryang Eoreumgol apples [4, 19, 24], and there are warnings that squid, a popular Korean fish species, could disappear due to climate change [122]. Climate change could be the biggest driver of inflation [136, 163], complicate refugee migration alongside conflicts [137], and exacerbate socioeconomic issues, such as putting the UK's net-zero ambitions to the test amid soaring living costs [162].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic and International Carbon Neutrality and Climate Adaptation Efforts: Innovations and Achievements
sections.content: Domestic and international efforts for carbon neutrality and climate adaptation are actively underway to address the climate crisis. Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO) and Korea Midland Power (KOMIPO) received ministerial and presidential commendations, respectively, at the 'Carbon Neutrality and Green Management Awards,' recognizing their achievements in greenhouse gas reduction and green management. KEPCO, in particular, achieved a 36.2% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions [11, 22, 27, 44, 49, 52, 54, 58, 64, 70, 80]. Various local governments and public institutions across the country are also engaged in diverse activities to implement carbon neutrality. Sunchang County reduced carbon emissions by 41 tons at its festival, and Gangnam-gu is encouraging citizen participation by hosting a 'Green Talk Concert' [30, 34, 35, 41, 42, 43, 46, 53, 59, 65, 66, 72, 74, 75, 79]. In terms of technological innovation, Ohoodoosilab introduced 'AI Carbon Management' technology at the UN Climate Change Conference [1], and research into low-carbon blended cement development and aquaculture alternatives like triploid oysters is ongoing [6, 31, 56, 109]. Furthermore, international cooperation is strengthening, with the APEC Climate Center supporting the establishment of an agricultural climate management system in Peru and KOICA opening smart greenhouses in the Philippines [12, 14, 18]. Various aspects of climate change solutions, including water management and gene-editing technologies, are being discussed both domestically and internationally [121, 123, 128, 134, 149].

sections.title: 🌱 Energy Transition and Policy Directions: Challenges and Opportunities
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy is accelerating globally, with positive changes observed, such as China's share of coal power generation falling below 50% for the first time [82]. The International Energy Agency (IEA) projects a 57% increase in global renewable energy capacity by 2031. Domestically, there is active movement, with Korea Southern Power (KOSPO) launching new renewable energy projects through private proposals, and LS Materials and LS Electric moving to secure leadership in the renewable energy and AI data center power grid stabilization markets [83, 84, 85, 86, 87, 88, 89, 91, 92, 93, 94, 95, 96, 98, 99, 100, 101, 103, 105, 107]. The automotive industry is collectively calling for regulatory framework adjustments and government-industry collaboration to accelerate the transition to carbon neutrality and autonomous driving [29, 37, 39, 40, 51, 61, 62, 67, 71, 73, 90, 153]. COP31 is also heavily betting on electrification as a solution to climate change [144, 155]. However, 34.9% of companies assessed carbon neutrality policy effectiveness as insufficient, citing a lack of support programs. The instability of wind power output, as seen in the Danish case, emphasizes the importance of early risk management in expanding renewable energy [36, 55, 97, 104]. Despite these challenges, continuous policy improvement and cooperation, such as discussions on renewable energy profit-sharing policies by Jeonnam Gwangju and the Basic Income Party, must be pursued to maximize the opportunities of the energy transition [102, 106, 115, 116, 117, 166].

briefing.closing: As we have seen in today's briefing, the world faces an unprecedented challenge in the climate crisis. With COP31 as a pivotal point, there is a strong and continuous demand for concrete action and accelerated energy transition. We hope that innovative efforts and cooperation, both domestically and internationally, will serve as a driving force to turn this crisis into an opportunity. This concludes today's climate briefing.
